Test for anemia and iron deficiency at referral, regularly during follow-up, and when
symptoms suggest anemia. Minimum testing frequency increases with CKD severity
(annually in CKD G3, twice yearly in G4, and every 3 months in G5 or dialysis).
For patients receiving hemodialysis, initiation of iron therapy is suggested if ferritin ≤
500 ng/ml (≤500 µg/l) and TSAT ≤30%. A proactive approach (regular maintenance
doses) is preferred over a reactive approach to ensure stable iron status and potential-
ly improve cardiovascular outcomes.
For patients not receiving dialysis or those receiving peritoneal dialysis, initiation of
iron is suggested at less stringent ferritin/TSAT thresholds, reflecting different iron
losses and inflammation burdens.
• ferritin <100 ng/ml (<100 µg/l) and TSAT <40%, or
• ferritin ≥100 ng/ml (≥100 µg/l) and <300 mg/ml (<300 µg/l), and TSAT <25%
• Hemodialysis: Intravenous iron is suggested over oral iron for efficiency and reduced
pill burden.
• CKD not receiving dialysis or CKD G5PD: Either oral or iv iron is suggested, and the
choice should be based on patient values, degree of deficiency, tolerability, availabili-
ty, and cost.
Consider withholding routine iron if ferritin >700 ng/ml or TSAT ≥40%, or during
systemic infection. A trial of iron could be given for people with high ferritin (>700
ng/ml) but low TSAT (<20%) provided that they also have severe anemia or high ESA
requirements This helps balance the benefits of treatment against theoretical risks of
iron overload or direct tissue toxicity.
Before initiating ESA or HIF-PHI therapy, address potentially reversible causes of
anemia including iron deficiency, inflammation, blood loss, hypothyroidism,
hyperparathyroidism, and nutritional deficiencies.
ESAs are suggested as the first-line treatment for anemia in CKD over hypoxia-induci-
ble factor–prolyl hydroxylase inhibitors (HIF-PHIs). While HIF-PHIs are effective, they
have not been shown to be safer than ESAs and their long-term risks and benefits
outside clinical trials are unknown.
Treatment decisions regarding iron, ESAs, HIF-PHIs, and red blood cell (RBC)
transfusions should be made together with patients, carefully weigh individual
patient values, preferences, symptoms, comorbidities, and both benefits and risks of
each therapeutic option.
For people with CKD G5HD or CKD G5PD, initiation of ESA therapy is suggested when
Hb is ≤9–10 g/dl (≤90–100 g/l; Figures 1 and 3). For those not receiving dialysis,
consider selecting the threshold for initiation based on symptoms, cardiovascular risk,
transfusion risk, and transplant candidacy rather than using a uniform threshold
(Figure 2).
In adults with anemia and CKD treated with ESAs, it is recommended to target
hemoglobin levels <11.5 g/dl (115 g/l) to avoid increased risks of stroke, cardiovascular
events, and thrombosis associated with higher targets.
Use RBC transfusions as part of a comprehensive strategy, not based on arbitrary Hb
thresholds but on clinical signs and symptoms. Professionals must prioritize avoiding
transfusions in transplant candidates to minimize the risk of allosensitization.
